label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/snapbug.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_medkit.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, C, D, C where the asset was C, A, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Front, back and side views all show a wheel: a ring rim, six spokes and a central hub, with the same outline in every view (front, back, top and the diagonal views). The rim is slightly polygonal, but nothing sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: Measured 32 by 32 by 5 units against the 32 asked, a 0.1% difference, well inside 15%.

M3.reason: The brief names a wheel with red paint worn to steel at the rim. The rim (steel), the spokes (red) and the hub (red, a short cylinder protruding both sides) are all present, and the rim's cross-section is round. Nothing named is missing.

M4.reason: Spokes and hub are painted red, the rim is steel-grey with lighter worn patches and some brown rust spots. This matches the brief's red paint worn to steel at the rim, with each region in its own colour and material.

M5.reason: Wear is visible on the rim: light chipped patches at about 3 and 9 o'clock in the front and back views, streaks on the steel, and a worn look on the red spokes. The wear sits where the brief puts it, at a sharpness close to the game's own props.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. Across four readings, the asset was never picked as the one not made by Valve (the judges picked D, C, D, C where the asset was C, A, B, D), so it passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The wheel stands upright, its face toward the front view, with the hub at the centre of the rim. The brief sets no facing, and the placement is sound.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors. At 372 triangles it is under the 422 that Half-Life's most-complex props of this kind and size use, so the triangle count is within the amended limit. Nothing visibly open: the spokes and hub join the rim, and the rim's small notches at about 3 and 9 o'clock read as chips, not holes.
